transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my daughter actually made the appointment for me. She was over last week—she just got this new job at the bank downtown, the one with the big glass windows? I always tell her she needs to dress warmer for that office, they keep the AC blasting all year. But anyway, she noticed... I came in because my eating has gotten all turned around for months now. Some days I just pick at a piece of toast and have my coffee, and other days... well, I'll be at the grocery store—they rearranged the aisles at my local market, which is so confusing, I couldn't find the canned beans for twenty minutes—and I'll just stand in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. It's just strange.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over these past months?

Well, I haven't really weighed myself... my scale in the bathroom is one of those old dial ones, you know? It belonged to my mother, and the little red line always seems to stick around the zero mark unless you tap it just right. She bought it at a yard sale back in the nineties from Mrs. Gable down the street. Mrs. Gable always had the best yard sales, she used to sell these beautiful embroidered tea towels... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, weight. I'm not sure if I've lost a lot of weight, it's just... like I said, the eating is all over the place. Some days it's just the toast, and then other days I'm buying all those bakery sweets. It's just turned around, you know? My clothes fit a little differently, maybe, but I mostly wear these loose cardigans now anyway because the draft in my house is terrible since they fixed the roof last spring...
Do you often feel guilty after eating those sweets or other foods?

Guilty? No, I wouldn't say I feel guilty about it. It's just food, you know? Though they really do put so much sugar in things these days. I was actually watching this program on the television the other afternoon about how they process sugar cane down in South America. They have these massive machines—huge metal things, just churning away out in the fields. It reminded me of the factory my neighbor, Mr. Henderson, used to work at. He made parts for airplanes or something like that before he retired. He has this beautiful golden retriever named Buster who always barks at the mailman. The mailman is new, by the way, a very polite young man, he always makes sure to put the letters all the way in the box so they don't get wet. It rained so much last Tuesday, didn't it? My poor petunias were completely drowned out in the front yard. But anyway... no, I don't really feel bad after I eat the bakery things.
Have you noticed your clothes fitting differently or falling off in the past few months?

Well, like I said, I mostly wear those loose cardigans anyway... I actually order them from this catalog that comes in the mail. The mail carrier—I mentioned him earlier, the polite young man—he always leaves the catalog right on the porch chair so it doesn't get ruined. They have the most beautiful knit sweaters in there for the autumn season. 

But about my clothes falling off... no, they aren't falling off exactly. I did have to pull the belt a notch tighter on my brown slacks the other day, though. It just goes back to what I was telling you when I first came in, about my eating being so turned around these past few months. Because when you're just picking at toast and coffee some days, and then other days you're standing in the bakery aisle buying all those sweets you don't even really want... well, your body just doesn't know what to do. I wore those brown slacks to the pharmacy, actually. Brenda, the pharmacist, she just had a baby girl... they named her Lily, which I think is just so precious. My aunt had a dog named Lily once, a little white poodle...
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your eating habits changed?

Well, like I was saying, it's just that my eating has been all turned around for months now. That's actually why I came in to see you. Because some days I just pick at my toast and have my coffee, and then other days... well, I'll find myself just standing right there in the bakery aisle at the grocery store, buying all these sweets that I don't even really enjoy eating. The grocery store, the one on Main Street, they just remodeled their whole bakery section. They put in these new glass display cases, very modern looking, with these bright lights that make everything look so shiny. It's almost too bright, really, it hurts my eyes a little bit if I look at it too long. My cousin Martha, she had terrible trouble with her eyes, she had to get those special tinted glasses... but yes, the eating is just completely turned around, so I suppose my weight might be doing the same thing, I just don't know for sure.
Have you noticed that your weight has decreased since your eating habits changed?

Well, decreased... I mean, I don't own a scale anymore. I threw it out years ago after I read this article in a magazine at the dentist's office. Dr. Evans is my dentist, he has the most beautiful saltwater aquarium in his waiting room. I could watch those little yellow fish swim around for hours. It's so calming, isn't it? Water just has that effect on people. My grandfather used to take me fishing down at the creek when I was a little girl... he had this old green tackle box that smelled like peppermint for some reason. 

But about my weight decreasing... it's just like I keep trying to explain, it's the eating that's the real problem. That's exactly why I made the appointment to come in here. My eating has just gotten all completely turned around for months now. I'll have days where I just sit there and pick at a piece of dry toast and sip my coffee, and I just can't bring myself to eat a real meal. And then, out of nowhere, other days I'll be standing right there in the middle of the bakery aisle, just filling my cart with all these sweets and pastries that I don't even really enjoy eating. It makes no sense at all. The bakery boxes are always tied with that little red string, though, which I always thought was a nice touch. I save the string sometimes to tie up the tomato plants in my garden... well, the ones the rabbits haven't gotten to yet, anyway.
Are there any activities you've stopped doing or find more difficult to do because of your eating habits?

Well, the activities... I still manage to get through the basic things for my aunt. I make sure she's settled. She has this lovely old armchair, it's upholstered in this floral pattern with tiny pink roses. It used to sit in my grandmother's sunroom. The sunroom had these big bay windows that let in all the morning light, and we'd sit there and drink tea... Earl Grey, mostly, though sometimes chamomile if it was later in the day. 

But, oh, because of the eating being so turned around... it has made things harder. Caregiving, and just staying involved in town, it all feels so much more difficult than before. I've missed a few of the church planning calls lately. We were supposed to be organizing the spring bake sale. Usually, I'm the one who coordinates the pie donations, because you have to make sure you don't end up with ten cherry pies and no apple. Apple is always the best seller, especially Mrs. Higgins' apple pie. She puts a secret ingredient in the crust—I think it's a splash of vinegar, but she won't tell a soul. 

I've also put off my projects for the county fair... and I've even had to ask the neighbors to cover things I used to handle so easily. Mr. Henderson next door, he's been so kind, he helped me with the trash bins last week. He has a golden retriever that just barks and barks at the mailman... the polite young man I mentioned earlier with the catalogs. But yes, it's just all gotten so much harder to keep up with.
Are you ever afraid of gaining weight?

Afraid of gaining weight? No, I wouldn't say I'm afraid of it... I don't really think about it like that. I mean, my clothes still fit the same way they always have. I've had this one blue wool sweater for, oh, it must be fifteen years now. I bought it at a little boutique downtown that closed last spring. It's a shame, really, the woman who ran it, Eleanor, she always had the most beautiful silk scarves in the window. She moved to Florida to be closer to her daughter. Her daughter just had twins, a boy and a girl, can you imagine? Twins run in my family, actually. My great-aunt had twins... but no, I'm not afraid of putting on weight or anything like that. It's just the eating itself that's so upside down right now.
Do you think your eating habits are influenced by a fear of gaining weight?

No, no, it's not a fear of gaining weight at all. I mean, I just said I'm not afraid of that, didn't I? It's just... the eating itself is what's so strange. Like I said about the bakery aisle. And speaking of the grocery store, they completely rearranged the aisles last week. I went in for coffee—just the regular roast, nothing fancy, I don't understand all those flavored coffees they have now, hazelnut and vanilla and what have you. Coffee should just taste like coffee, don't you think? Anyway, I went in, and they had moved all the canned goods over to where the paper towels used to be. It took me twenty minutes just to find a can of crushed tomatoes for my aunt's soup. She likes the soup with the little star-shaped pasta, pastina, I think it's called. But no, the eating is just... all over the place. It has nothing to do with worrying about my weight.
Have you noticed that your weight has decreased significantly since your eating habits changed?

Well, decreased significantly? I wouldn't say my weight has dropped a whole lot, but I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. Some days I just pick at a piece of toast and have my coffee... speaking of coffee, I finally found my favorite mug. It had been missing for weeks. It's this sturdy ceramic one with a picture of a lighthouse on it. My sister bought it for me when we took a trip up the coast to Maine about ten years ago. Oh, the seafood there was just incredible. We had clam chowder at this little place right on the water, and you could hear the seagulls squawking outside. 

But yes, my eating is just a mess. Like I was saying, some days it's just toast, and other days... well, other days I find myself standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. I bought a whole box of those frosted sugar cookies last week. The ones with the thick pink frosting and the sprinkles? They look so pretty in the package, but they always taste a bit like cardboard, don't they? I don't know why they still sell them. The bakery section used to be so much better when Mr. Miller ran it. He made these fresh cinnamon rolls every Saturday morning, and the whole store would smell like butter and spice. But he retired... oh, it must have been five years ago now. He bought an RV and decided to travel the country with his wife. I think they went to the Grand Canyon first. But anyway, my weight... I haven't really noticed a huge drop, it's just the eating itself that's so upside down.
Have you lost a noticeable amount of weight recently?

I feel like we're going in circles a bit, doctor. Like I just said, no, I haven't noticed a big drop in my weight or anything like that. I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. It's just so unpredictable. Some days I just pick at my toast and coffee... which actually reminds me, I really need to get a new toaster. The lever on mine gets stuck halfway down, so you have to stand there and hold it down if you want the bread to actually brown. 

It's a heavy silver one, I think I got it at Sears years and years ago. Do you remember when Sears used to send out that massive catalog in the mail? The Wish Book, they called it. My mother used to let my sister and me circle things in it for Christmas with a red marker. I always circled the bicycles, even though we lived at the top of this terribly steep hill and riding a bike would have been completely impractical. We had a neighbor, Mr. Henderson, who tried to ride a ten-speed down that hill once and ended up right in Mrs. Gable's prize-winning rose bushes. She was furious. 

But anyway, no, I haven't lost a noticeable amount of weight. It's just the eating itself being so strange, going from barely managing toast to standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy.
Do you find that your eating habits change in response to your emotions?

Emotions? Oh, I don't know if it's emotions. I just... I came in because my eating has gotten all turned around for months now, like I've been trying to explain. It's just so erratic. Like I said, some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I'm standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

Speaking of sweets, my neighbor brought over a fruitcake for the holidays last year. I know people always make jokes about fruitcake, how it's heavy enough to use as a doorstop and all that, but this one actually wasn't bad. She soaked it in rum, I think. Or maybe brandy. Her husband, Tom, he collects vintage decanters, so they always have some kind of liquor sitting out on that beautiful mahogany sideboard they have in their dining room. I've always wanted a sideboard like that, but my dining room is much too small. If I put one in there, you wouldn't even be able to pull the chairs out to sit down! We'd all have to eat standing up, like we were at a cocktail party or something. 

But anyway, no, I don't think it's about my emotions. It's just that my appetite is completely upside down these days.
Do you think your mood affects how much or what you eat?

Doctor, I feel like I keep saying the same thing over and over. I don't know about my mood affecting it. I just came in because my eating has been completely turned around for months now. Like I've mentioned, some days I just pick at my toast and coffee, and other days I'm in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even like. 

Speaking of the bakery, I saw the strangest thing there the other day. A woman had her little dog in the shopping cart, right where you put the groceries! It was one of those tiny, fluffy white dogs—a Bichon Frise, maybe? My aunt Edna used to have a Bichon. She named him Snowflake, which was terribly unoriginal, but she loved that dog more than anything. She used to knit him little sweaters for the winter. Bright red ones, usually. Edna was always knitting. She made me a scarf once that was so long it wrapped around my neck three times and still dragged on the floor. I wore it anyway, just to make her happy when she visited. 

But no, I don't think it's my mood. It's just my eating being so upside down, going from toast to sweets for no reason at all.
Do you feel like you're eating less because you're not interested in food or because you're trying to avoid gaining weight?

Doctor, I feel like you're not hearing me. It's not about trying to avoid gaining weight or not being interested. Like I've been saying, I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. It's completely unpredictable. Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I'm standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

I bought these lemon squares last time. I don't even like lemon! It always reminds me of the furniture polish my grandmother used to use. She had this beautiful antique dining set, cherry wood, I think. She made us polish it every single Sunday before dinner. We'd have to rub it in little circles until our arms ached. If you missed a spot, she'd know. She had eyes like a hawk, that woman. She could spot a speck of dust from across the room. She used to say, "A clean house is a sign of a clear mind." I always wondered if that meant my mind was a mess, because my house is definitely not spotless right now. I keep meaning to dust the living room, but I just look at the Swiffer and think... what's the point? It's just going to get dusty again anyway. 

But anyway, no, I'm not trying to avoid gaining weight. My eating is just completely upside down.
Do you think you might be eating less on some days because you're just not that interested in food?

Doctor, I really don't know how else to explain this to you. We keep going in circles. It's not about being interested or not interested in food. I'm here, like I've told you three times now, because my eating has gotten all turned around for months. It makes no sense. One day I'm just picking at a piece of toast and having coffee, and the next day I'm standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

I bought a whole box of those powdered sugar donuts last week. The ones that get the white powder absolutely everywhere. You take one bite and suddenly you look like you've been caught in a blizzard. My brother used to eat those all the time when we were kids. He'd purposely blow the powdered sugar across the table at me just to make me mad. Our mother would yell at him, but she never really punished him. He was the golden boy, you know? Played baseball, got good grades. He works in insurance now. Lives out in Ohio. I haven't seen him since... well, since before the holidays. He sent a card, though. One of those photo cards with his perfect family wearing matching sweaters in front of a fireplace. I don't even know where you buy matching sweaters for five people. A catalog, maybe? 

But no, it's not a lack of interest. It's just entirely upside down, toast one day, sweets the next.
Do you think your emotions play a role in whether you eat more or less on a given day?

Doctor, I feel like we are having two entirely different conversations. Emotions? I don't... I don't know why we keep trying to pin this on my emotions or my mood or my interest. I'm telling you, I came in because my eating has gotten all turned around for months now. That's it. Some days I pick at toast and coffee, and other days I stand in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

I don't even like sweets that much, honestly. My husband, though, he had a terrible sweet tooth. He could eat a whole pint of butter pecan ice cream in one sitting. Butter pecan. I always thought it tasted like frozen sawdust, but he loved it. He used to buy it from this little dairy stand out on Route 9. They had a giant plastic cow on the roof. You could see it from a mile away. I wonder if that place is still open. They used to paint the cow different colors for the holidays. Orange for Halloween, wearing a little Santa hat for Christmas. It was so tacky, but the kids loved it when they were little. My daughter used to beg to go see the "Santa Cow." She's out in California now, working for some tech company. I don't really understand what she does. Something with computers and the internet. 

But no, it's not my emotions making me eat. It's just my eating being completely upside down, like I've been saying.
Do you ever feel like you're not hungry at all on the days when you only pick at your toast and coffee?

Doctor, I... I don't know why this is so hard to get across. We're just going around and around again. It's not about being hungry or not being hungry. Like I keep trying to explain, I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. That's the whole thing. Some days I pick at toast and coffee, and other days I stand in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

I actually bought these awful cherry turnovers yesterday. The filling was so bright red, it looked like paint. It stained my tongue just looking at it. It reminded me of this lipstick my Aunt Carol used to wear. "Fire engine red," she called it. She wore it everywhere, even to the grocery store or just sitting around her house. She used to blot it on a tissue and leave these perfect little red lip prints in the wastebasket. I used to think it was so glamorous when I was seven. She had this big, fluffy white cat named Snowball that would shed everywhere. You couldn't sit on her couch without standing up looking like you were wearing a mohair sweater. I'm actually highly allergic to cats. My eyes swell up like golf balls. 

But anyway, no, it's not about not being hungry. My eating is just completely upside down, just like I've been saying this whole time.
Do you feel like you're eating less on some days because food just doesn't taste good to you?

Doctor, I really don't know how many different ways I can say the exact same thing to you. We are literally just spinning our wheels here. It has nothing to do with food tasting good or bad. I don't know why we are so focused on the taste of things or being hungry or my emotions. I am sitting here telling you, for the fourth time, that I came in because my eating has gotten all turned around for months now. That is what is happening. Some days I pick at toast and coffee, and other days I stand in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

I bought a whole package of those stale-looking cinnamon rolls just the other day. The ones in the plastic clamshell container that always pops open in your grocery bag and gets icing on everything else. I got icing all over a bunch of celery. Who puts icing on celery? It reminded me of this terrible diet my neighbor Linda tried back in the 90s. The cabbage soup diet, I think it was. She made her whole house smell like boiled socks for a week straight. She was always trying these crazy fads. Once she bought this expensive vibrating belt machine that she swore was shaking the fat off her hips. It just made a horrible racket that you could hear through the walls, like a lawnmower running in the living room. She ended up selling it at a yard sale for five dollars to a guy who thought he could use the motor for a go-kart. 

But no, it's not the taste. It's just my eating being completely upside down, exactly like I've been telling you.
Do you feel like you're not interested in eating on the days when you only pick at your toast and coffee?

Doctor, are you even listening to me? I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall today. We are literally just going in circles. It has nothing to do with being interested or not interested! I don't know how to make this any clearer. I am telling you, my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. That's the whole story. Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I'm standing in the bakery aisle loading up on sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

Speaking of coffee, I actually dropped my favorite mug this morning. Smashed into a million pieces all over the linoleum. It was this ugly brown ceramic thing I got at a yard sale in... oh, it must have been 1998. The guy running the sale had this huge collection of ceramic frogs. Just hundreds of them, all over his lawn. Some were playing little instruments, like a banjo or a tuba. I always wondered who sits around making tiny tubas for ceramic frogs. It seems like a very specific hobby. Like building ships in bottles. My uncle Arthur tried to build a ship in a bottle once, but he got his finger stuck in the neck of the glass and had to go to the emergency room to get it cut off. The bottle, I mean, not his finger. Though he did lose a toe later on in a lawnmower accident. He was wearing sandals while cutting the grass, which is just asking for trouble if you ask me. 

But anyway, no, it's not about my interest in food. It's exactly what I've been saying this whole time, my eating is just completely upside down.
Do you feel like you're not interested in eating on the days when you only pick at your toast and coffee?

Doctor, I... I don't know why we keep doing this. I feel like a broken record, and you're just asking the exact same question again. It's not about being interested or not interested in the food! I've been trying to tell you, my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. That's the only way I know how to explain it. Some days I just pick at toast and coffee, and other days I'm standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets I don't even really enjoy. 

I bought these powdered sugar donuts the other day, and the powder got all over my black pants. It looked like I'd been rolling around in flour. It reminded me of when I tried to make homemade pasta from scratch during that big snowstorm back in 2010. I had flour on the ceiling, flour on the dog... the dog was a black lab mix named Buster. He loved the snow. He would jump into the snowbanks and disappear, just a little black tail wagging out of the white. We had to shovel a path just so he could go to the bathroom. My husband bought this massive snowblower that year, but he could never get it to start on the really cold days. He'd just stand out there pulling the cord and cursing until the neighbors closed their windows. 

But no, it's not about interest. My eating is just upside down, just like I said.
